title: Attach card brackets to the internal boards
body: Screw two card brackets to each internal board with M2.5x5 pan head screws: usually the flight controller, the battery board and a payload board. Leave the screws snug but not tight. You square the brackets in the next step.
gap: Only the battery board's card brackets are modeled. The flight controller is a placeholder shape, and the payload slot shows Electra's mass block.

title: Square the brackets in one frame half
body: Loosen the board-to-bracket screws. Mount the board in one frame half so the frame pulls the brackets out to their full extent. Tighten the board-to-bracket screws, then take the board back out. Repeat for each board.

title: Install the feet
body: Fit the feet to the frame with the M2 screws and lock nuts, nylon side of the nut facing into the satellite. Put the two feet with deployment switches on diagonally opposite corners. Fit the feet on both halves now. The second half joins in step 7.
gap: The feet screws and lock nuts are not modeled.

title: Install the L-brackets
body: Screw the four L-brackets to the frame half with M2.5x5 button head screws. Button heads matter here: the solar faces sit on top of these screw heads. Drive screws into press-in nuts straight and level, and do not exceed 0.59 N·m.

title: Mount the boards in the frame half
body: Screw each board's card brackets to the frame half at the height you want. The usual layout puts the flight controller at the top and the battery board at the bottom. A payload goes in the middle, or below the flight controller on standoffs.

title: Install and route the wire harnesses
body: Plug the harnesses into the boards: face ports, foot switches, remove-before-flight, burn wire and the top cap. Route the wires through the cutouts at the sides of the boards so the solar faces can sit flush later.
gap: The wire harnesses are not in the 3D model yet.

title: Install the other frame half
body: Bring in the second half, with its feet already fitted, and screw it to the L-brackets and the remaining card bracket holes. Leave the screws loose enough that the frame can still shift. You square it in the next step.

title: Square the frame in the assembly jig
body: Slide the frame back and forth through the 3D printed jig until the rails measure 100 mm x 100 mm. Then, without taking it out of the jig, tighten every screw. For a flight unit, take each screw out in turn, dip it in blue Loctite and put it back.
gap: The assembly jig is not in the 3D model yet.

title: Connect the faces and run a functional test
body: Plug the remaining boards into the far ends of the harnesses: the four XY solar faces, the Z− face and the antenna board on top. With everything connected but not yet screwed down, power up and run the functional test.

title: Close out with the Z boards
body: Screw on the Z boards first: the Z− solar face at the bottom and the antenna board on top. They hold the frame in its square shape while you fit the sides.

title: Close out with the XY boards
body: Screw the four XY solar faces onto the sides with M2.5x5 screws. The kit is assembled.
